intro: In coding, a word is changed by a fixed rule. Work out the rule from the example, then use it on the new word, or undo it to find a hidden word.

tips.title: Write the letters as numbers
tips.body: Put A = 1 … Z = 26 under both words. The gap between them shows the shift: +3 means every letter moves 3 places.

tips.title: Opposite letters add up to 27
tips.body: In the A ↔ Z code, A + Z = B + Y = 27. So a letter's code is 27 minus its place: G (7) → 20, which is T.

tips.title: Check the order too
tips.body: If the code uses the same letters as the word, the word may just be written backwards, or pairs of letters may have swapped places.

tips.title: Growing steps
tips.body: If the shift changes from letter to letter (+1, +2, +3…), write the step under each letter before you work anything out.

tips.title: Decoding? Undo the steps
tips.body: To go from a code back to a word, undo each step in reverse order: if the code was shifted and then reversed, un-reverse first, then shift back.

tips.title: Tables of words and codes
tips.body: When the digits are jumbled, compare two words that share exactly one letter: the one digit their codes share belongs to that letter.
